introH2: 🏖️ What is Lamai Beach like, and which zone should you stay in?
introHtml: Lamai is Koh Samui's second most famous beach after Chaweng, on the island's southeast coast just below it — a long white-sand beach lined with restaurants, bars, massage shops and a Sunday walking-street night market, but with a far more relaxed feel than Chaweng, and the island's landmark Grandfather & Grandmother Rocks at its southern end · Lamai's charm is that it doesn't have one single face — the central strip is the main beach with both beachfront resorts and walkable shops and nightlife, while the northern and southern ends fold into small quiet coves where resorts sit privately, and on the hill above the bay there's even a luxury pool-villa resort with full sea views · That range means Lamai has stays from a couple of thousand baht a night to eighteen-thousand-plus, each a genuinely different experience — book the wrong zone and the mood of the trip shifts: you wanted to step out onto the sand but ended up in a rocky cove waiting for a shuttle, or you wanted quiet but got a room facing the bar street · One more thing to know: Lamai's beach changes with the season — at times (especially the year-end monsoon) the surf picks up and seaweed washes in, so many resorts keep a sea-view pool as the main swim · This guide gathers 8 Lamai Beach hotels we've reviewed in depth, covering every budget — all built from reading real guest reviews, with the good and the honest caveats spelled out, prices compared across 3 booking sites, and direct links to book
mrtHtml: Koh Samui has no rail transit — you'll get around by rental car, rented scooter, songthaew (red trucks), or Grab (available but limited at times) · Lamai sits on the island's southeast coast, about 10–13 km (20–30 minutes) from Samui Airport (USM) and 15–20 minutes from Chaweng · The zones in this guide: Beachfront, central Lamai — step out to the sand, walkable to the walking street, restaurants, bars and a 7-Eleven (Pavilion, Samui Jasmine, Aloha, Lamai Wanta) · Northern end / coves — quiet and private; several are small bays with rocks in the sand, so guests mainly use the pool, with a free shuttle to a sandy beach (Renaissance, Outrigger) · Rocky cove, southern end — a quiet boutique on a rocky bay not made for swimming, but walkable to the village (Rocky's) · Private hill above Lamai Bay — luxury sea-view pool villas, reached by car/buggy, about 3 minutes' drive from Lamai Beach (Banyan Tree) · After dark Lamai has bars and a night market but stays quieter than Chaweng; light sleepers should ask for a room facing the garden or sea, set back from the road

entries.storyHtml: If you want one Lamai stay that combines real quiet with a walkable village, plenty of reviews point to Rocky's Boutique Resort (Veranda Collection) — a boutique of 67 rooms plus 3 pool villas set on a private rocky cove at the southern end of Lamai, ringed by the natural boulders it's named after, and the highest score in this list at 9.2 · Real guest reviews consistently praise the romantic, quiet mood, the two free-form pools facing the sea, the seaside restaurant The Dining Room, and staff who remember your name — enough to earn a Travellers' Choice · The honest caveats: the beach out front is a rocky cove, the sand isn't fine and it's not made for swimming (there's a free shuttle twice daily to Lamai and Chaweng beaches), the resort steps down a slope with stairs, and some décor is starting to show its age · Best for couples, honeymooners, and anyone who values atmosphere and service over a wide sandy beach at the door
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, pick Premier Ocean View or above, or the Beachfront with Plunge Pool, for full cove views and a private plunge pool · Check the shuttle times on day one if you plan to swim at a sandy beach · Ask for a room near the central areas if stairs are hard going · And compare the direct-booking perks against the price across all 3 sites before you book
pros: Highest score in this list at 9.2 · a quiet private cove, yet still walkable to the Lamai village
Two free-form sea-view pools, seaside dining at The Dining Room, and a fresh breakfast
Warm staff who remember guests and help plan trips — a Travellers' Choice winner (per reviews)
Better value than the island's top-brand resorts for the experience you get
cons: The beach out front is a rocky cove with coarse sand, not made for swimming (free shuttle to a sandy beach)
The resort steps down a slope with a fair amount of stairs and ramps
Some rooms' décor is aging · the shuttle runs only twice a day (per reviews)

entries.storyHtml: If you want a big-chain resort without sitting in the middle of Chaweng's bustle, Renaissance Koh Samui Resort & Spa, part of Marriott Bonvoy, comes up often — a 5-star resort and spa of 78 rooms and pool villas set on a private twin-cove bay at the northern end of Lamai, scoring 8.9 from 2,151 reviews, the largest review base in this list · Real guest reviews praise the seaside infinity pool and 50-metre lap pool, the bayside Tawann restaurant, the Quan Spa many call a trip highlight, and even entry-level rooms with an outdoor jacuzzi · The honest caveats: the beach out front mixes rock and coral and goes shallow at low tide, so most guests use the pools (there's a free shuttle to a sandy beach), the resort steps down a slope with stairs, and in-resort food and drink run high by chain standards · Best for couples, Marriott Bonvoy members, and families who want a quiet, private stay
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, pick Deluxe Sea View or above, or a pool villa, for bay views and a private pool · Bonvoy members should compare booking direct with the chain for upgrade and points perks · Reserve the spa and dinner at Tawann ahead in high season, as slots fill fast · And check the beach-shuttle times on day one
pros: A quiet, very private bay · the largest review base here at 2,151
Seaside infinity pool + 50m lap pool · even entry rooms have an outdoor jacuzzi
Marriott Bonvoy standards and points · Quan Spa and Tawann earn steady praise (per reviews)
More affordable than the island's very top brands in a private-bay setting
cons: The beach out front mixes rock and coral, shallow at low tide, not made for swimming
The resort steps down a slope with a fair amount of stairs and ramps
It's outside the village, and in-resort food and drink run high (per reviews)

entries.name: Outrigger Koh Samui Beach Resort

entries.storyHtml: If this trip is with the kids and you want a beachfront resort with things to do all day, Outrigger Koh Samui Beach Resort comes up often — a colonial-style 4-star on Lamai's northern beachfront (formerly Manathai), 146 rooms and suites, scoring 8.6 from 1,829 reviews · Real guest reviews praise the several pools, one with a slide and a shallow kids' area, the Coral Kids Club, the seaside Edgewater restaurant, and staff whose service score sits at 9.1 · The honest caveats: the beach out front runs shallow and can get seaweed some seasons, so most guests swim in the pools, the main road cuts the resort in two so some rooms are across the street, and in-resort food runs high · Best for families with kids and couples who want an easy beachfront with good service
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a beachside room at booking if you'd rather not cross the main road · If you're a family and plan to use the lounge, weigh the price gap for a Club room against Voyager 47 Club perks · Grab a poolside lounger early in high season · And compare a breakfast-included package with eating out in the Lamai village
pros: A family beachfront with several pools + a slide + the Coral Kids Club
Spacious rooms, soft beds, handsome colonial style · staff score 9.1 (per reviews)
Walk to the Lamai walking street · Club rooms use the Voyager 47 lounge
Fresh, varied breakfast at Mala Kitchen · lovely seaside Edgewater
cons: The beach out front is shallow with seasonal seaweed, not for deep swims
The main road cuts the resort in two, so some rooms are across the street
In-resort food runs high · poolside loungers fill fast in the afternoon (per reviews)

entries.name: Pavilion Samui Villas & Resort
entries.badge: 🏖️ Beachfront in the village · private pool villas
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Beachfront, central Lamai · walk to the night market
entries.addr: 124/24 Moo 3, Maret, Lamai Beach, Koh Samui
entries.storyHtml: If you want to sleep right on the sand in central Lamai and still walk to the market and restaurants, Pavilion Samui Villas & Resort comes up often — a contemporary-Thai resort of about 70 rooms and villas set right on the beach in the heart of the strip, where you step out of the garden onto the sand, scoring 8.4 from 971 reviews with a 9.2 location score on Booking · Real guest reviews praise the two big sea-view pools plus a kids' pool, the beach bar, a breakfast that changes daily, and options from a hydro-pool room up to a Beachfront Pool Villa with a private pool · The honest caveats: it's been refurbished in phases so some room types are aging with older, noisier AC at night, a few rooms have open-plan bathrooms without full walls, and it sits in the village where you'll hear the bars in the evening · Best for anyone who wants both sand at the door and shops within a stroll, plus couples after a pool villa at a lighter price than the top brands
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, take a Beachfront Pool Villa or Plunge Pool Suite for a private pool and full sea views · Ask for a room or villa facing the garden or sea and set back from the bar street if you're a light sleeper · Check whether the rate includes breakfast before booking · And book in low season, when prices clearly drop
pros: Truly beachfront in the village · walk to the Sunday market, restaurants, bars and a 7-Eleven
Two big sea-view pools + a kids' pool · a beach bar · 9.2 location score (per reviews)
Private pool villas and hydro-pool rooms at a lighter price than the top brands
Friendly, helpful staff scoring 9.2 · a breakfast that changes daily
cons: Some room types are aging, with older AC that's noisy at night
It's in the village, so street-facing rooms can hear the bars at night
A few rooms have open-plan bathrooms without full walls · 8.2 value score (per reviews)

entries.storyHtml: In the middle of Lamai's lively strip of restaurants and bars, Samui Jasmine Resort plays the opposite hand — a beachfront boutique of just 35 rooms whose buildings step down a tropical garden to the sea, scoring 8.9, among the highest here · What real guest reviews single out most is the seaside saltwater pool facing the Gulf that stays open late, the white-sand beach out front with free loungers, and staff who live by a 'you are our family' motto — plus an uncrowded seaside breakfast buffet · The honest caveats: it's a small boutique with none of the big-resort facilities, some rooms are aging and a few have glass-walled bathrooms, and being in the village means some nights you'll hear the bars · Best for couples and small families who want a beachfront in the village on a controlled budget and value the boutique feel and service
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, take Deluxe Building Sea View or a jacuzzi villa for sea views and more privacy · Ask for a room facing the garden or sea if you're a light sleeper · Book with the seaside breakfast, which earns steady praise · And grab a poolside lounger early
pros: Beachfront in the village · a seaside saltwater pool open late, steps from the sand
Score 8.9 · warm 'like family' staff are the highlight (per reviews)
Very clean rooms, linens and pool area · an uncrowded seaside breakfast
White-sand beach out front with free loungers and umbrellas
cons: A small boutique — no kids' club or full gym like the big resorts
Some rooms are aging · a few have glass-walled bathrooms (per reviews)
It's in the village with bars nearby; weekend nights you may hear music in street-facing rooms

entries.storyHtml: On a Lamai stretch lined with restaurants and massage shops, Aloha Resort Koh Samui is a long-standing Thai-style beachfront resort — teak gabled buildings, 74 rooms scattered through a tropical garden that slopes to the sand, scoring 8.0 from about ฿1,800/night, the cheapest here · Real guest reviews praise the free-form seaside pool with a jacuzzi and kids' area, the beachside pool bar, the leafy garden, and warm, helpful staff · The honest caveats to know first: the rooms are old and showing wear, hot water can be weak in some rooms, sockets are few, and Tripadvisor rates it only 3.3/5 for room condition (Trip.com gives 8.3) · Best for couples and budget families who value the beachfront location and price over how new the rooms are, especially those who'll mainly be at the pool, on the beach, and out of the resort
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget allows, take a Grand Deluxe or a more recently renovated sea-view room for clearly better condition · Ask to see the room at check-in, and if the hot water or a musty smell is off, ask to switch · Ask for a quieter room away from the bar street if you're a light sleeper · And pack a power strip and mosquito repellent
pros: Truly beachfront from about ฿1,800 — the cheapest in this list
Free-form seaside pool + jacuzzi + kids' pool + beachside pool bar
Leafy tropical garden · warm, helpful staff (per reviews)
Walk to the Lamai walking street, restaurants and massage shops
cons: Rooms are old and showing wear · Tripadvisor 3.3/5 for condition
Weak hot water in some rooms, few sockets, some rooms lack a tea/coffee set
The beach changes with the season, with surf and seaweed at times (per reviews)

entries.storyHtml: If you want to turn a Lamai trip into a no-holds-barred pool-villa retreat, Banyan Tree Samui is the area's luxury landmark — a 5-star with 88 villas on a private hill above Lamai Bay, every one with its own sea-facing infinity pool, scoring 9.5, the highest in this list (from 147 reviews) · Real guest reviews love the privacy of swimming in your own pool all day barely seeing another soul, the private beach with free water toys, the Banyan Tree Spa with its Rainforest hydrotherapy, and the seaside Thai restaurant Saffron · The honest caveats: it's the priciest here (from about ฿18,000/night), the resort is built on a steep hill so you rely on a buggy, it sits apart about 3 minutes' drive from Lamai Beach, and the private beach has rocks at low tide · We've placed it at the end of the list as the upgrade pick — best for honeymooners and those who mean to spend the trip inside the resort
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If your budget stretches, take an Ocean View villa or above, as some lower villas have views screened by trees · Use the free buggy freely — call anytime, it usually arrives in 4–5 minutes · Book a table at Saffron and pair the Rainforest with a massage in advance · And in high season (Dec–Mar) prices climb fast, so lock a free-cancellation rate early

entries.storyHtml: Closing the list is a budget pick that's genuinely beachfront — Lamai Wanta Beach Resort, a 3-star set right on the sand in central Lamai, with a sea-facing infinity pool ringed by a leafy tropical garden, from about ฿2,000/night, scoring 8.0 · Real guest reviews praise the seaside infinity-pool view you can step straight onto the beach from, the location within walking distance of the Sunday market and restaurants (a 7-Eleven about 50 metres away), and garden bungalows that are brighter and roomier than the lower rooms in the block · The honest caveats: it's a simple, aging 3-star, the rooms in the 400 zone sit near the bars with music late at night, and the leafy garden means a fair few mosquitoes · Note: it's now rebranded as The Hive Hotel, so you may see both names — check the address matches before booking · Best for anyone who wants a village beachfront and a sea-view pool at a price that's easy to swallow
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room away from the 400-zone bar street if you're a light sleeper, and if you can, request a garden bungalow — brighter and roomier · Poolside chairs are limited, so grab one early · Pack mosquito repellent · And double-check the name/address (The Hive Hotel) matches before you book

noteHtml: 📌 Note: All prices are approximate starting rates for standard rooms outside peak season and can change by date and season — always check the live price and compare 3 sites before booking · Scores and standout points in this guide come from reading real guest reviews on booking platforms; we did not stay ourselves · In Koh Samui's high season (December–February) prices rise clearly and small stays like Samui Jasmine and Rocky's fill first, so plan ahead · Lamai's beach changes with the season — the year-end monsoon brings bigger surf and some seaweed, so many resorts use a sea-view pool as the main swim · Cove stays (Rocky's, Renaissance) and hillside ones (Banyan Tree) involve stairs or a buggy/shuttle, so they suit people who walk comfortably · Getting around the island is mainly by rental car, scooter, songthaew and Grab · Article by ThailandAddict.com
faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Lamai Beach hotels, Koh Samui

faq.q: ❓ Which Lamai Beach hotel is best?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget · For score-to-price, Rocky's Boutique Resort at 9.2, a quiet cove boutique, leads the affordable tier · For a big chain on a private bay, Renaissance Koh Samui at 8.9 (Marriott Bonvoy) · With kids, Outrigger Koh Samui has several pools and the Coral Kids Club · For a private luxury pool villa with no price ceiling, Banyan Tree Samui at 9.5 is the highest here

faq.q: ❓ How much do Lamai Beach hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, from about ฿1,800–18,000 per night · The budget end is Aloha Resort from ฿1,800 and Lamai Wanta from ฿2,000 · Mid-range is Pavilion ฿2,800, Samui Jasmine ฿2,900 and Rocky's ฿3,500 · Upper mid is Outrigger ฿5,000 and Renaissance ฿6,500 · And the luxury pool villas at Banyan Tree from ฿18,000 · All are approximate starting rates outside peak; high season (December–February) climbs clearly

faq.q: ❓ How is Lamai different from Chaweng, and who is it for?
faq.a: Lamai is the next beach south of Chaweng, about 15–20 minutes' drive, but the feel is different — Lamai is quieter and more relaxed, with a Sunday walking street, restaurants and bars, but nothing like Chaweng's buzz, and the landmark Grandfather & Grandmother Rocks at its south end · Chaweng is the island's nightlife and shopping hub, while Lamai suits families, couples and people who really came to relax · If you want nightlife every night, Chaweng is easier, or stay in Lamai and drive over occasionally

faq.q: ❓ Which Lamai Beach hotel is best for families?
faq.a: The most family-focused is Outrigger Koh Samui ฿5,000 — several pools with a slide and a shallow kids' area, the Coral Kids Club, a games room, and connecting Family rooms for parents and kids · On a lighter budget, look at Pavilion Samui and Aloha Resort, both with a kids' pool and beachfront in the village · Bigger families or groups can take Pavilion's 2-bedroom villa or Lamai Wanta's Family Deluxe Villa · Banyan Tree suits families with the budget for a private pool villa

faq.q: ❓ Can you swim at Lamai Beach, and which stays are truly on a swimmable sandy beach?
faq.a: The central Lamai strip is white-sand and swimmable, and the stays right on that sand are Pavilion, Samui Jasmine, Aloha and Lamai Wanta — step out and walk onto the beach · But the northern and southern coves, like Rocky's and Renaissance, are bays with rock and coral in the sand, not made for swimming, so guests use a sea-view pool and there's a free shuttle to a sandy beach · Banyan Tree has a small private beach that's swimmable but has rocks at low tide · Note: the year-end monsoon brings bigger surf and some seaweed

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book, and how do you get around?
faq.a: In Koh Samui's high season (December–February) book 1–2 months ahead, especially small stays like Samui Jasmine (35 rooms) and Rocky's, which fill first; in low season 1–2 weeks is fine and prices drop a lot · Getting there: from Samui Airport (USM) it's about 20–30 minutes to Lamai, by taxi, hotel car or Grab · On the island, renting a car or scooter is popular, and songthaews (red trucks) run the main roads · Every platform offers free cancellation — lock that in if plans aren't firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price
